idea.body: Multiplying two polynomials means every term in one meets every term in the other. For (x + 2)(x + 3), that is four small products: x times x, x times 3, 2 times x, and 2 times 3. Add those four pieces together: x^2 + 3x + 2x + 6, which combines to x^2 + 5x + 6. An area model shows this as a rectangle split into four boxes, one for each small product. A monomial times a polynomial works the same way, just with fewer pieces to add.

figure.alt: An area model for (x + 2)(x + 3): four boxes for x times x, x times 3, 2 times x, and 2 times 3.

steps: Every term in the first factor meets every term in the second.
x times x gives x^2. x times 2 gives 2x.
3 times x gives 3x. 3 times 2 gives 6.
Add the four pieces: x^2 + 2x + 3x + 6.
Combine the middle terms: x^2 + 5x + 6.

figure.alt: An area model for (x + 3)(x + 2): four boxes for x times x, x times 2, 3 times x, and 3 times 2.

ways.name: The area model
ways.when: Use this default method for multiplying two binomials.
steps: Draw a rectangle split into four boxes, one for each pair of terms.
x times x gives x^2. x times 1 gives x.
4 times x gives 4x. 4 times 1 gives 4.
Add the four boxes: x^2 + x + 4x + 4.
Combine the middle terms: x^2 + 5x + 4.
ways.trap: Forgetting one of the four boxes, usually one of the two middle terms.

ways.name: Distribute twice
ways.when: Use this when you prefer working with the brackets instead of drawing a box.
steps: Distribute the first factor across the second: x times (x - 2) and 5 times (x - 2).
x times (x - 2) gives x^2 - 2x.
5 times (x - 2) gives 5x - 10.
Add the two results: x^2 - 2x + 5x - 10.
Combine the like terms: x^2 + 3x - 10.
ways.trap: Distributing only the first term and skipping the second term across the bracket.

ways.name: The special product patterns
ways.when: Use this when the two factors are identical, or a sum and difference of the same terms.
steps: Recognise the pattern: (x + 6)^2 is a times a, plus twice a times b, plus b times b.
Square the first term: x times x gives x^2.
Double the product of the two terms: 2 times x times 6 gives 12x.
Square the last term: 6 times 6 gives 36.
ways.trap: Squaring each term separately and forgetting the middle doubled term.
